# 1 Enoch Chapter 90 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records key verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 90 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 90:2 — 'great horn' — identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-great-horn-of-one-of-those-sheep" | Literal; the horn belongs to a sheep |
| LOGOS | "a great horn of one of those sheep" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "a great horn sprouted on one of the sheep [Judas Maccabeus]" | Adds identification in brackets |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS clean text. The 'great horn' = Judas Maccabeus is universally accepted by scholars (cf. 1 Macc 2:1-5; 3:1-9; the horn imagery echoes Dan 7-8 where horns = rulers). The identification is placed in SOPHIA notes, not embedded inline.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Identification in notes.

---

## 90:13 — 'that man sitting on a lofty throne of judgment'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "that-man-sitting-on-a-lofty-throne-of-judgment" | Literal; 'that man' = God or a divine figure |
| LOGOS | "that man sitting on a lofty throne of judgment" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the man [God/the Ancient of Days] sitting on a high throne of judgment" | Adds identification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'that man sitting on a lofty throne of judgment.' The 'man' (Ge'ez: sab') sitting in judgment here is identified with the divine judge — almost certainly alluding to Daniel 7:9-14 (the Ancient of Days). Whether this is God directly, an angelic figure, or an anticipation of the Son of Man figure developed in 1 En 37-71, is debated. The identification is placed in SOPHIA notes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Identification in notes.

---

## 90:27 — 'white bull' = the Messiah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-white-bull-was-born, with-large-horns" | Literal; the Messianic figure appears as a white bull |
| LOGOS | "a white bull was born, with large horns" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "a white bull born with great horns [the Messiah]" | Adds identification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS clean text. The white bull = the Messiah is the standard interpretation: the Messiah restores the primordial state (Adam was a white bull); the great horns signal kingly/priestly authority. The identification is in SOPHIA notes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 90:28 — 'all became white bulls' — eschatological transformation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-all-became-white-bulls" | Literal; universal eschatological transformation |
| LOGOS | "they all became white bulls" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "they all became white bulls [all of creation restored to Adamic perfection]" | Adds interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS clean text. The transformation of all into white bulls is the most remarkable eschatological image in the text: the entire created order returns to its primordial state — white like Adam, the first white bull. This is not merely the salvation of Israel but the transformation of all creation. The interpretation is in SOPHIA notes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 90:31 — Enoch's weeping

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-wept-with-a-great-weeping-and-my-tears-stayed-not-till-I-could-no-longer-endure-it" | Literal; maximum emotional intensity |
| LOGOS | "I wept with a great weeping and my tears stayed not until I could no longer endure it" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "I wept — a great, uncontrollable weeping" | More emotionally direct |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The cognate construction 'wept with a great weeping' is a Semitic intensifier and should be preserved. PNEUMA's 'uncontrollable' adds an interpretation not in the source. The tears that 'stayed not' = kept flowing is more literal and more vivid than 'uncontrollable.'

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Semitic intensifier preserved.

---

## 90:18 — 'folded up that old house'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-folded-up-that-old-house" | Unusual image: the house is literally 'folded' — like a tent |
| LOGOS | "they folded up that old house" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "they dismantled the old house" | 'Dismantled' loses the specific 'folding' image |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'they folded up that old house.' The 'folding up' image is significant: it evokes the dismantling of a tent, reinforcing the connection to the Tabernacle (the Tent of Meeting). The old house (Jerusalem/Temple) is packed up like a tent — to be replaced by a permanent, superior structure (the New Jerusalem). PNEUMA's 'dismantled' loses this nuance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Tent/folding imagery preserved.

---
